subject: Recap: Dedicated capacity discussion & next steps
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acme-health.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity discussion (today)

Hi Marissa/David,

Thanks again for the demo and the focused discussion today - really helpful. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying questions so we can align with procurement: 

Pain points / goals we discussed:
- Current inference on shared endpoints is inconsistent during peak hours (95th p95 spikes causing customer-facing latency issues).
- Need guaranteed throughput for peak windows (avg 12 reqs/sec, spikes to 40 reqs/sec) for our document-parsing pipeline.
- Data isolation and residency: PHI-containing payloads must remain in our VPC; we need private control plane or equivalent.
- Cost predictability for budgeting - committed monthly cost is preferred.

Initial asks for Redwood Dedicated:
- Reserved capacity: aiming at a starting point of 8x A100-class GPUs (ability to scale + burst)
- Isolation: VPC peering or private link and SOC2 evidence
- SLA targets: 99.9% uptime and p95 latency under 150ms for short responses (we understand token length affects this)

Questions:
1) Can you provide a short written recap of the proposed config, high-level pricing, and expected lead time for onboarding?
2) How does the autoscaling/bursting work with reserved capacity - do we get automatic extra nodes during short spikes?
3) Is HSM/KMS integration for key management supported?

Next steps from Acme: run this recap by procurement and security. Carlos (cc'd) will handle procurement. We hope to decide on committed capacity by mid-December.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Health

-----
Elena T.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acme-health.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity discussion (today)

Hi Elena - great talking yesterday. Appreciate the clear priorities; below is a concise recap and proposed next steps so procurement/security have something to review.

Recap (what we discussed)
- Recommended configuration: Dedicated cluster with 8x A100-class GPUs (reserved).
  - Baseline throughput: supports ~12 req/s steady with headroom for spikes to ~40 req/s with autoscale/burst.
  - Autoscale policy: add up to 2 additional nodes (equivalent to +4 A100 capacity) for sustained spikes >30s. Burst capacity can be configured to allow short-term increases beyond reserve.
- Isolation & security: Private control plane + VPC peering (or PrivateLink), optional on-prem connector. KMS integration supported; HSM available for enterprise keys.
- Performance targets & SLA: Redwood can target 99.9% uptime for Dedicated clusters. P95 latency depends on payload size and token lengths; for your doc-parsing workload we estimate p95 ~120-180ms for short responses on the recommended config. We'll include latency SLO language in the SOW with measurement windows.
- Data residency & compliance: deployment in US regions only for Acme; SOC2 report attached.

Proposed commercial structure
- Committed monthly reserved capacity (8x A100) + metered burst. We will provide a pricing estimate in the formal SOW.
- Typical onboarding timeline: 3-5 weeks after SOW signature and PO (includes network setup, authentication, and initial load testing).

Attachments (attached to this email)
- Redwood_Dedicated_SOW_v2.pdf (proposal and initial pricing ranges)
- SOC2_Report_Q3_2026.pdf

Next steps / mutual action plan
1) Redwood to provide final SOW and pricing (this week).
2) Acme to review SOW w/ procurement & security - procurement to confirm PO terms (Carlos).
3) Technical kickoff & network prep (target week of Jan 4, 2027).
4) Sandbox validation and canary rollout plan (we'll propose a brief canary run prior to full cutover).

Please let me know if I missed anything important. I can jump on a 20-minute call with procurement/security if that helps accelerate.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0142

- Canary rollout: we want a short canary (1-2 days) to validate reliability before full cutover. Can we include a canary plan in the SOW?

If you can add those points into the SOW (or an appendix) that would be ideal. Otherwise looks good - Carlos will coordinate PO discussions.

Elena

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity discussion (today) - technical clarifications & next steps

Hi Elena / Carlos - quick technical follow-up and confirmation from my side. Thanks for the thorough notes - they match what we'd planned. A few details to lock into the SOW: 

1) Canary & rollout plan
- We'll run a 48-hour canary in your sandbox with traffic mirroring to verify latency and autoscale behavior. If metrics pass (p95, error rate), we proceed to phased cutover. Canary plan will be an appendix in the SOW.

2) Autoscaling/burst behavior
- Reserved nodes remain until PO term ends. Autoscale will add pre-warmed burst nodes for short spikes; bursts beyond pre-warmed capacity are subject to availability and billed at the agreed burst rate (we'll define burst rate in the SOW).

3) Network & isolation
- VPC peering or PrivateLink supported. We'll need one week to coordinate firewall rules and CIDR allocations. Private control plane option ensures customer-managed network access for control-plane calls.

4) KMS / HSM
- We support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations. HSM-backed CMKs are supported for enterprise customers; we'll include a short integration checklist for security.

5) SLA & credits
- Target SLA: 99.9% monthly uptime for the Dedicated cluster. SLA credits will be provided as service credits per the SOW tier (we'll include explicit credit table).

Next steps
- Marissa: finalize SOW (incorporate canary appendix + billing clarity).
- Redwood: send DocuSign link for SOW + initial pricing by EOD (we've attached the draft SOW here for reference).
- Acme: confirm target onboarding window (week of Jan 4, 2027).

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/abc123-redwood-acme-sow

Happy to hop on a short technical call if your security team prefers.

Thanks,
David Kim

Redwood Inference
